title: 669. Greece vs. Persia: The Battle of Marathon (Part 2)

sentences.zh: 说到底，历史上的每一个王朝都归结为两个重要因素：抱负与行动。

sentences.en: And a classic example of this from British history, the rise of the House of Wessex,
sentences.zh: 英国历史上一个典型的例子就是威塞克斯王朝的崛起，

sentences.en: the family of Alfred the Great and his heirs, who, between them, established the United Kingdom of England.
sentences.zh: 也就是阿尔弗雷德大帝及其继承人的家族，他们共同建立了英格兰联合王国。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great story, isn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 没错，这是一个很棒的故事，不是吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: A great lesson in leadership, I think, for anybody.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对任何人来说都是一堂很好的领导力课程。

sentences.en: So Alfred and his heirs, they marry idealism and pragmatism.
sentences.zh: 所以阿尔弗雷德和他的继承人们，他们将理想主义与实用主义结合在了一起。

sentences.en: They're brilliant at alliances.
sentences.zh: 他们非常擅长结盟。

sentences.en: They're brilliant at managing power.
sentences.zh: 他们非常擅长驾驭权力。

sentences.en: They're brilliant, of course, at managing their money, which is a key part of political leadership.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们也非常擅长理财，这是政治领导力的关键部分。

sentences.en: And of course, we are all reaping the rewards of their wisdom and foresight.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们现在都在享受他们智慧和远见带来的成果。

sentences.zh: 当您需要迈出下一步时，您可以信赖劳合社，我们随时准备为您提供支持。

sentences.zh: 因为从新企业到新家园，再到人生的新篇章，在几代人的希望与雄心支持下，

sentences.en: As the Athenians crossed deeper into no man's land, the first arrows began to hiss down upon them.
sentences.zh: 当雅典人深入无人区时，第一批箭矢开始呼啸着向他们射来。

sentences.en: Then, raising the monstrous weight of their shields to protect their chests, the hoplites did at last begin to run.
sentences.zh: 随后，重装步兵们举起沉重的盾牌护住胸口，终于开始奔跑。

sentences.en: Simultaneously, as though the phalanx were some ferocious cornered creature stiffening its bristles as it turns to face its foe,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，方阵就像一只凶猛的困兽，在转身面对敌人时竖起了鬃毛，

sentences.en: those in the front three ranks lowered and aimed their spears in preparation for the coming collision.
sentences.zh: 前三排的士兵放低并瞄准了长矛，为即将到来的碰撞做准备。

sentences.en: By now, with some 150 yards still to travel, a storm cloud of arrows and slingshot was breaking over them,
sentences.zh: 此时，距离还有约一百五十码，一阵箭雨和弹丸构成的风暴在他们头顶倾泻而下，

sentences.en: thudding into their shields, bouncing off their helmets, striking the odd hoplite in the thigh or through the throat.
sentences.zh: 重重地砸在盾牌上，从头盔上弹开，偶尔有重装步兵的大腿或喉咙被击中。

sentences.en: But still the Athenians, braving the black rain, only quickened their pace.
sentences.zh: 但雅典人冒着黑色的箭雨，反而加快了步伐。

sentences.en: Those of the enemy directly in their path had already begun scrabbling to erect wicker defences, as they realised, to their horror, that the wall of shields and iron-tipped spears,
sentences.zh: 挡在他们前进道路上的敌人已经开始手忙脚乱地架设柳条防御工事，因为他们惊恐地意识到，那堵由盾牌和铁头长矛组成的墙，

sentences.en: far from providing easy pickings for their bowmen as they had at first imagined, was not going to be halted.
sentences.zh: 远非他们最初想象的那样能让弓箭手轻易收割，而是根本无法被阻挡。

sentences.en: A hundred yards.
sentences.zh: 一百码。

sentences.en: Fifty.
sentences.zh: 五十码。

sentences.en: Twenty.
sentences.zh: 二十码。

sentences.en: Ten.
sentences.zh: 十码。

sentences.en: Then, as the Athenians' war cry, a terrifying allulation, rose even above the thundering of their feet upon the dry earth,
sentences.zh: 接着，当雅典人的战吼——一种令人胆寒的呼喊——盖过了他们双脚踏在干涸土地上的雷鸣声，

sentences.en: the cacophony of clattering metal and the screams of the panic-stricken enemy, the phalanx crunched into the Persian lines.
sentences.zh: 盖过了金属碰撞的嘈杂声和惊慌失措的敌人的尖叫声时，方阵狠狠地撞进了波斯人的阵线。

sentences.en: So what a dramatic moment that is.
sentences.zh: 真是个戏剧性的时刻。

sentences.en: That is the moment when the Athenian phalanx charges and smashes into the ranks of the invading Persians
sentences.zh: 那一刻，雅典方阵发起冲锋，粉碎了入侵的波斯军队，

sentences.en: at the Battle of Marathon, as narrated by a friend of the show, Dan Brown, in his book, Persian Fire.
sentences.zh: 正如本节目的朋友丹·布朗在他的著作《波斯之火》中所讲述的马拉松战役那样。

sentences.en: So rude.
sentences.zh: 太粗鲁了。

sentences.en: We are in the late summer of 490 BC.
sentences.zh: 我们现在处于公元前490年的夏末。

sentences.en: Everything hangs in the balance.
sentences.zh: 一切都悬而未决。

sentences.en: And who better to tell the story than the man who wrote those words?
sentences.zh: 还有谁比写下这些文字的人更适合讲述这个故事呢？

sentences.en: Dan Brown himself, Tom Holland, is with us on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 丹·布朗本人，汤姆·霍兰德，正与我们一起录制播客。

sentences.en: So, Tom, we advertised this at the end of the previous episode, where we did the build-up to the Battle of Marathon, the war between the Persians and the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们在上一集的结尾预告过，当时我们讲述了马拉松战役的准备阶段，即波斯与希腊之间的战争。

sentences.en: We advertised this as one of the great showdowns, not just in ancient history, but in all history.
sentences.zh: 我们将其宣传为不仅是古代史上，而且是全人类历史上最伟大的对决之一。

sentences.en: It's a battle that proved a template for so many clashes to come, seen even today, especially, I think, in America, by historians who teach at military academies.
sentences.zh: 这场战役为后来的许多冲突提供了模板，即使在今天，特别是在美国，那些在军事学院任教的历史学家们依然这样认为。

sentences.en: We'll often say it's the great titanic showdown between democracy and despotism.
sentences.zh: 我们经常说这是民主与专制之间伟大的泰坦式对决。

sentences.en: So you've got the Athenians on one side, and on the other, you have the most powerful man on earth,
sentences.zh: 所以你一边是雅典人，另一边是地球上最有权势的人，

sentences.en: Darius the Great, the King of Kings, the Shah of Shars, the Emperor of Persia.
sentences.zh: 大流士大帝，万王之王，众王之王，波斯皇帝。

sentences.en: Why is this battle so celebrated?
sentences.zh: 为什么这场战役如此出名？

sentences.en: Well, I think there are a number of reasons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为有几个原因。

sentences.en: The first is that, I mean, it is the first battle in European history that we can kind of reconstruct.
sentences.zh: 首先，我的意思是，这是欧洲历史上我们能够进行某种程度还原的第一场战役。

sentences.en: So that is courtesy of Herodotus, who recounts it in considerable detail.
sentences.zh: 这要归功于希罗多德，他在书中对此进行了相当详细的叙述。

sentences.en: There are gaps, and so there are various interpretations of the battle.
sentences.zh: 当然存在空白，因此对这场战役有各种不同的解读。

sentences.en: And the interpretation you're going to hear today is mine.
sentences.zh: 而你今天听到的解读是我的版本。

sentences.en: But I think on the fundamentals, people are pretty agreed what happened.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在基本事实上，人们对发生的事情相当一致。

sentences.en: And so that is a firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这还是头一遭。

sentences.en: I think also it has always been seen as one of history's most decisive battles.
sentences.zh: 我认为它一直被视为历史上最具决定性的战役之一。

sentences.en: It really matters who wins in this clash.
sentences.zh: 在这场冲突中，谁获胜确实至关重要。

sentences.en: And this begins with the Athenians themselves, who, and it's a massive spoiler alert here, the Athenians win it.
sentences.zh: 这始于雅典人自己，而且——这里要剧透一下——雅典人赢了。

sentences.en: They've been massively outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 他们当时在人数上处于绝对劣势。

sentences.en: They're facing an enemy that has never been defeated by Greeks before.
sentences.zh: 他们面对的是一支从未被希腊人击败过的敌人。

sentences.en: But they've done it, and they've saved Greece.
sentences.zh: 但他们做到了，他们拯救了希腊。

sentences.en: And decades, centuries, maybe even millennia, I mean, the Greeks still go on about it.
sentences.zh: 几十年、几个世纪，甚至几千年过去了，希腊人依然津津乐道。

sentences.en: This sense that they have saved freedom is something that they never leave alone.
sentences.zh: 那种他们拯救了自由的感觉，是他们永远不会放下的执念。

sentences.en: And perhaps it's a little bit like the British going on about the Battle of Britain.
sentences.zh: 也许这有点像英国人谈论不列颠战役一样。

sentences.en: There's a slight kind of similar quality to that, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为两者之间有一种微妙的相似之处。

sentences.en: But it's not just the Greeks who have said that the Battle of Marathon was decisive.
sentences.zh: 但不仅仅是希腊人认为马拉松战役具有决定性意义。

sentences.en: So this is John Stuart Mill in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 这是19世纪约翰·斯图尔特·密尔的观点。

sentences.en: The Battle of Marathon, he wrote, even as an event in English history, is more important than the Battle of Hastings.
sentences.zh: 他写道，马拉松战役，即便作为英国历史上的一个事件，也比黑斯廷斯战役更重要。

sentences.en: If the issue of that day had been different, the Britons and the Saxons might still have been wandering in the woods.
sentences.zh: 如果那天的结果不同，不列颠人和撒克逊人可能至今还在森林里游荡。

sentences.en: And what he means by that is that the Battle of Marathon is the battle that enabled the West to become the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 他的意思是，马拉松战役是使西方成为西方的战役。

sentences.en: It enabled Europe to become properly European.
sentences.zh: 它使欧洲真正成为了欧洲。

sentences.en: And by extension, it's the triumph of liberty over slavery and of democracy over despotism, as you said.
sentences.zh: 推而广之，正如你所说，这是自由战胜奴役、民主战胜专制的胜利。

sentences.en: But is it not the case that had the Persians won the Battle of Marathon, people in Britain would have been wearing trousers much earlier than they were?
sentences.zh: 但如果波斯人赢得了马拉松战役，英国人会不会比历史上更早穿上裤子？

sentences.en: I know, shocking.
sentences.zh: 我知道，这很令人震惊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think the notion of it being the victory of freedom is something that, as you say, is still current today.
sentences.zh: 我认为它作为自由胜利的观念，正如你所说，在今天依然具有现实意义。

sentences.en: I think particularly, as you said, in right-wing circles, perhaps in America.
sentences.zh: 我认为特别是在右翼圈子里，也许是在美国。

sentences.en: But it's not just people on the right who have celebrated Marathon.
sentences.zh: 但不仅仅是右翼人士在庆祝马拉松。

sentences.en: So Byron, back in the beginning of the 19th century, who would end up dying for freedom,
sentences.zh: 拜伦，在19世纪初，他最终为自由而死，

sentences.en: dying for Greece, kind of the prototype of the supporter of the struggle for self-determination.
sentences.zh: 为希腊而死，某种程度上是支持民族自决斗争者的原型。

sentences.en: He visited the Plain of Marathon at a time when Greece was being ruled by the Ottomans.
sentences.zh: 他在希腊被奥斯曼帝国统治时期访问了马拉松平原。

sentences.en: And he then wrote kind of famous lines,
sentences.zh: 然后他写下了著名的诗句，

sentences.en: The mountains look on Marathon, and Marathon looks on the sea.
sentences.zh: 群山俯瞰马拉松，马拉松俯瞰大海。

sentences.en: And musing there an hour alone, I dreamed that Greece might still be free.
sentences.zh: 独自在那儿沉思一小时，我梦想着希腊或许仍能自由。

sentences.en: For standing on the Persians' grave, I could not deem myself a slave.
sentences.zh: 站在波斯人的坟墓上，我无法认为自己是个奴隶。

sentences.en: So the question of whether it really was decisive, whether it really was the triumph over something called the West, over something called the East, of freedom over despotism,
sentences.zh: 所以，关于它是否真的具有决定性，是否真的是西方战胜了东方，自由战胜了专制，

sentences.en: I mean, these are important questions, and we will come to them in due course.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些都是重要的问题，我们会在适当的时候讨论它们。

sentences.en: But I think more pressing is the details of the battle itself, the kind of incredible heart-stopping drama of this incredible clash.
sentences.zh: 但我认为更紧迫的是战役本身的细节，这场不可思议的冲突中那种令人心跳加速的戏剧性。

sentences.en: So before we come to that, a reminder of what we covered in our previous episode.
sentences.zh: 在进入正题之前，先回顾一下我们在上一集的内容。

sentences.en: So Darius is the king of Persia, the king of kings, and he rules this immense empire, which now stretches from Macedon,
sentences.zh: 大流士是波斯国王，万王之王，他统治着这个庞大的帝国，现在从马其顿，

sentences.en: from the foothills of Mount Olympus, all the way to the Indus.
sentences.zh: 从奥林匹斯山的脚下，一直延伸到印度河。

sentences.en: Darius is committed to having his vengeance on the Athenians, who had backed a revolt against Persian rule in Ionia,
sentences.zh: 大流士一心要向雅典人复仇，因为他们支持了爱奥尼亚反抗波斯统治的起义，

sentences.en: which is on the far side of the Aegean from Greece, so what is now Turkey.
sentences.zh: 爱奥尼亚位于爱琴海远离希腊的一侧，也就是现在的土耳其。

sentences.en: Darius had sent a naval expedition commanded by his nephew, a guy called Artafernes, and by Datis, who is a Mede who specializes in Greek affairs.
sentences.zh: 大流士派出一支由他侄子阿塔弗涅斯和达提斯指挥的海军远征军，达提斯是一位专门处理希腊事务的米底人。

sentences.en: He knows how to fight them, but he also knows how to negotiate with them, and he's probably the guy who's really in command.
sentences.zh: 他不仅知道如何与他们作战，也知道如何与他们谈判，他很可能才是真正的指挥官。

sentences.en: The Persian task force has sailed across the Aegean.
sentences.zh: 波斯特遣部队已经横渡了爱琴海。

sentences.en: It has already sacked the city of Eretria, which had joined Athens in attacking Darius's empire, and now Eretria has been burnt to the ground.
sentences.zh: 它已经洗劫了埃雷特里亚城，该城曾加入雅典攻击大流士的帝国，现在埃雷特里亚已被夷为平地。

sentences.en: Its people have been taken as slaves, and it is the turn of Athens.
sentences.zh: 它的人民被沦为奴隶，现在轮到雅典了。

sentences.en: But the task force, as it sails down the coastline of Attica, is heading not directly for Athens itself, but for the Bay of Marathon.
sentences.zh: 但特遣部队在沿着阿提卡海岸航行时，并没有直接前往雅典，而是前往马拉松湾。

sentences.en: And the reason for that, I think, is that Datis does not wish to attempt an opposed landing.
sentences.zh: 我认为原因在于达提斯不想尝试强行登陆。

sentences.en: That's always the most kind of difficult task for an amphibious force.
sentences.zh: 对于两栖部队来说，这永远是最困难的任务。

sentences.en: And if he heads for Phalarum, which is the port that serves Athens, then obviously that would be inevitable.
sentences.zh: 如果他前往雅典的港口法勒隆，那么显然那是不可避免的。

sentences.en: That's what he would be facing.
sentences.zh: 那将是他必须面对的情况。

sentences.en: So for people who have only a vague sense of the geography of Attica, which is the kind of area of land dominated by Athens,
sentences.zh: 所以对于那些对阿提卡地理只有模糊概念的人来说，阿提卡是雅典统治的陆地区域，

sentences.en: if you think of it as the head of a horse which is reaching down to drink from a trough, sticking out from mainland Greece,
sentences.zh: 如果你把它想象成一匹马的头，正伸向水槽喝水，从希腊大陆伸出来，

sentences.en: Marathon lies on the opposite eastern side of that peninsula from Athens.
sentences.zh: 马拉松就位于那个半岛与雅典相对的东侧。

sentences.en: And so there are good reasons for the Persian task force to head there.
sentences.zh: 所以波斯特遣部队前往那里是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: There's a very long beach onto which the Persian ships can be hauled up.
sentences.zh: 那里有一片很长的海滩，波斯船只可以拖上岸。

sentences.en: There's a very long scimitar-shaped plain on which the Persians can make their base, and which crucially is perfect for the operation of their cavalry.
sentences.zh: 那里有一片长长的弯刀形平原，波斯人可以在那里建立基地，而且至关重要的是，这非常适合他们的骑兵作战。

sentences.en: And also from Marathon, it is possible to get to Athens.
sentences.zh: 而且从马拉松出发，是有可能到达雅典的。

sentences.en: So there's a road which leads from the south of the plain up the foothills.
sentences.zh: 有一条路从平原南部通往山脚。

sentences.en: It bifurcates and one road goes inland, one road goes along the coast, around the mountains that separate Marathon from Athens.
sentences.zh: 它分叉开来，一条路通往内陆，一条路沿着海岸，绕过将马拉松与雅典隔开的山脉。

sentences.en: And this is, it means that if the Persians can get onto that road, then they will be able to march on Athens without too much trouble.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果波斯人能走上那条路，他们就能毫无阻碍地向雅典进军。

sentences.en: Now, what if the Athenians come out of Athens and advance to Marathon to meet with the Persians in battle?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果雅典人走出雅典，前往马拉松与波斯人交战会怎样？

sentences.en: Well, the Persians are very confident if that happens that they will have the victory.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果发生这种情况，波斯人非常有信心他们会获胜。

sentences.en: As we said, they're strong in cavalry.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，他们骑兵强大。

sentences.en: The Greeks, who rely entirely on heavy infantry, have no cavalry at all.
sentences.zh: 完全依赖重装步兵的希腊人根本没有骑兵。

sentences.en: Marathon as a flat plane is ideally suited to the operation of cavalry.
sentences.zh: 马拉松作为平坦的平原，非常适合骑兵作战。

sentences.en: And not once in 50 years of Greco-Persian warfare has a Greek army been able to defeat the Persians in pitched battle.
sentences.zh: 在五十年的希腊-波斯战争中，希腊军队从未在正面战场上击败过波斯人。

sentences.en: So the Persians have every reason to be confident.
sentences.zh: 所以波斯人有充分的理由自信。

sentences.en: So why would the Athenians do that when they could stay?
sentences.zh: 那么雅典人为什么要在可以留守的情况下这样做呢？

sentences.en: Surely, if you're an Athenian commander, the obvious thing to do is to say, why don't we stay?
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你是雅典指挥官，最显而易见的事情就是说，我们为什么不留下来？

sentences.en: Why don't we wait for the Persians to come, bring them on, we'll stay in our city and withstand a siege and eventually they'll go home.
sentences.zh: 我们为什么不等着波斯人来，引诱他们，我们留在城里抵御围攻，最终他们会回家的。

sentences.en: Well, if they do that, then the Persians are confident as well that they will win because they are almost certain that the city will end up being betrayed.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果他们这样做，那么波斯人也很有信心他们会赢，因为他们几乎可以肯定这座城市最终会被背叛。

sentences.en: The Persians have a lot of experience of dealing with the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 波斯人处理希腊人的经验非常丰富。

sentences.en: They know that there are very fractious people given to kind of violent class tensions, tensions, rivalries among their leading men, all kinds of things like that.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这些人非常分裂，容易产生激烈的阶级紧张、矛盾、领导人之间的竞争，以及各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: And so it's very easy for the Persians to foster tensions.
sentences.zh: 所以波斯人很容易煽动紧张局势。

sentences.en: And it's already worked with Eretria, the city that they have just sacked, because that city had been betrayed by two of the leading aristocrats.
sentences.zh: 这在他们刚刚洗劫的埃雷特里亚城已经奏效了，因为那座城市被两名主要贵族背叛了。

sentences.en: The gates had been opened.
sentences.zh: 城门被打开了。

sentences.en: And so there is no reason to think that the same dirty tricks wouldn't work in Athens.
sentences.zh: 所以没有理由认为同样的卑鄙手段在雅典行不通。

sentences.en: And evidence of the fact that there are Athenians who are willing to work with the Persians is there in the form of the man who has actually led them to Marathon,
sentences.zh: 有雅典人愿意与波斯人合作的证据，就在于那个实际上带领他们来到马拉松的人身上，

sentences.en: because he is an Athenian and he is the former Tyrannos, the former autocratic strongman of the city, this guy called Hippias who had been expelled back in 510.
sentences.zh: 因为他是一个雅典人，而且是前僭主，即该市前独裁强人，这个叫希庇亚斯的人，他在公元前510年被驱逐。

sentences.en: And he's now 80 years old and he hasn't been back to his native city for two decades now.
sentences.zh: 他现在已经80岁了，已经二十年没有回到他的故乡了。

sentences.en: He'd gone and taken refuge with the local Persian governor.
sentences.zh: 他去寻求当地波斯总督的庇护。

sentences.en: The governor had demanded the Athenians take him back and they had said no way.
sentences.zh: 总督要求雅典人接纳他，他们拒绝了。

sentences.en: Hippias does not see himself as a traitor.
sentences.zh: 希庇亚斯并不认为自己是叛徒。

sentences.en: He's convinced that the only way that Athens can be saved is if the Athenians can be brought to submit to the Persians.
sentences.zh: 他坚信拯救雅典的唯一方法就是让雅典人屈服于波斯人。

sentences.en: And so he sees himself as the person who's the kind of ideal middleman.
sentences.zh: 所以他把自己看作是理想的中间人。

sentences.en: And actually the night before the Persian fleet sets sail for Marathon, he dreams that he's sleeping with his mother.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在波斯舰队启航前往马拉松的前一天晚上，他梦见自己与母亲同寝。

sentences.en: And this is a sign that he is going to be reunited with his homeland.
sentences.zh: 这是一个他将与祖国团聚的征兆。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: I'm not sure Dr. Freud would agree with that interpretation perhaps, but this is the interpretation that the Greeks give it.
sentences.zh: 我不确定弗洛伊德博士是否会同意这种解释，但这正是希腊人给出的解释。

sentences.en: And sure enough, the next day Hippias is present when the Persian fleet draws up at Marathon.
sentences.zh: 果然，第二天波斯舰队在马拉松靠岸时，希庇亚斯就在场。

sentences.en: The keels of the ships are dragged up onto the sands.
sentences.zh: 船的龙骨被拖上了沙滩。

sentences.en: Hippias steps down.
sentences.zh: 希庇亚斯走下船。

sentences.en: He is back on attic soil, ready as he sees it to try and bring the Athenians into the light of the Persian king's favour.
sentences.zh: 他回到了阿提卡的土地上，正如他所见，准备尝试让雅典人沐浴在波斯国王的恩宠之下。

sentences.en: Will you talk about the Athenians and the light?
sentences.zh: 你会谈论雅典人和光吗？

sentences.en: So in very Lord of the Rings,
sentences.zh: 所以非常有《指环王》中《王者归来》的风格，雅典人一听到消息，一旦海岸上的人们得知波斯人正在登陆，

sentences.en: Return of the King style, the Athenians, as soon as they've heard the news, as soon as news has reached people on the coast that the Persians are landing,
sentences.zh: 他们就点燃了一个巨大的烽火台，不是吗，

sentences.en: they've lit a giant beacon, haven't they,
sentences.zh: 彭特利孔山。

sentences.en: Mount Pentelecon.
sentences.zh: 那是马拉松和雅典之间的中间点，用来传递消息。

sentences.en: So that's midway between Marathon and Athens to communicate the news.
sentences.zh: 烽火点燃了。

sentences.en: The beacons are lit.
sentences.zh: 烽火点燃了。

sentences.en: Athens calls for aid.
sentences.zh: 雅典请求援助。

sentences.en: Great scenes.
sentences.zh: 场面宏大。

sentences.en: And presumably,
sentences.zh: 而且可以想见，

sentences.en: I mean, this is an age where of rumour and exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是一个充满谣言和夸大其词的时代。

sentences.en: So there must be the most tremendous rumours and...
sentences.zh: 所以一定会有极其惊人的传言，还有……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Mass panic.
sentences.zh: 大规模的恐慌。

sentences.en: Paranoid fantasies about the size of the Persian army.
sentences.zh: 关于波斯军队规模的偏执幻想。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: These terrifying Asiatic hordes who have landed on the sacred soil of Attica.
sentences.zh: 这些登陆阿提卡神圣土地的可怕亚洲大军。

sentences.en: And even though probably these reports are exaggerated, it is clear from the first reports that the Athenians are going to be significantly outnumbered, maybe two to one,
sentences.zh: 尽管这些报告很可能被夸大了，但从最初的消息来看，雅典人显然将处于明显的劣势，也许是二比一，

sentences.en: maybe even three to one.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能是三比一。

sentences.en: We're not entirely sure.
sentences.zh: 我们不太确定。

sentences.en: And so you're right.
sentences.zh: 所以你是对的。

sentences.en: Of course, there are people who say, this is mad.
sentences.zh: 当然，有人会说，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: We can't go out and confront them.
sentences.zh: 我们不能出去与他们对抗。

sentences.en: We should stay behind our walls.
sentences.zh: 我们应该待在城墙后面。

sentences.en: But actually, even before that beacon is lit, the decision has already been taken to go out and confront the invaders in the field.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，甚至在烽火点燃之前，就已经决定要出城在战场上迎击入侵者了。

sentences.en: And the man who had pushed this course in the assembly of the democracy and had it voted on
sentences.zh: 而在民主集会上推动这一方针并付诸表决，

sentences.en: and passed as an official resolution of the Athenian people is the city's most proficient campaigner against the Persians, the city's great mead fighter, as he's called,
sentences.zh: 并作为雅典人民的正式决议通过的人，是该城对抗波斯人最精锐的战士，也就是人们所说的该城伟大的米德战士，

sentences.en: Miltiades, because he has fought with and against the Persians.
sentences.zh: 米太亚得，因为他曾与波斯人并肩作战，也曾与他们交战。

sentences.en: He understands how they work.
sentences.zh: 他了解他们的运作方式。

sentences.en: He understands how their military operations are conducted.
sentences.zh: 他了解他们的军事行动是如何进行的。

sentences.en: And so his plan, the moment that the Persians have landed at Marathon, which is where Miltiades had expected they would land,
sentences.zh: 所以他的计划是，在波斯人登陆马拉松的那一刻——这也是米太亚得预料他们会登陆的地方——

sentences.en: is to march at top speed to that southern kind of mountain at the southern end of Marathon
sentences.zh: 以最快的速度行军到马拉松南端的那座山，

sentences.en: and to block the road that otherwise will enable the Persians to get to Athens from Marathon.
sentences.zh: 并封锁那条波斯人本可以从马拉松前往雅典的道路。

sentences.en: And if they can get there in time, then they will be able to bottle the Persians up on the plain of Marathon
sentences.zh: 如果他们能及时赶到，就能将波斯人困在马拉松平原上，

sentences.en: and thereby stop the Persian cavalry from taking that road and fanning out across Attica.
sentences.zh: 从而阻止波斯骑兵利用那条路向阿提卡全境扩散。

sentences.en: It's actually a little bit like Harold, you know, wanting to get to Hastings to stop the Norman cavalry from breaking out.
sentences.zh: 这其实有点像哈罗德，你知道，想要赶到黑斯廷斯去阻止诺曼骑兵突围。

sentences.en: It's kind of similar kind of strategy.
sentences.zh: 这是一种类似的策略。

sentences.en: So the beacon is lit.
sentences.zh: 于是烽火点燃了。

sentences.en: People see the flame.
sentences.zh: 人们看到了火焰。

sentences.en: There's a tremendous scene, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 场面非常壮观，不是吗？

sentences.en: Blow this great trumpet.
sentences.zh: 吹响这支大号角。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They summon men to the mustering ground, which is a sort of exercise ground, which has been dedicated to Apollo.
sentences.zh: 他们召集人们到集结地，那是一个专门献给阿波罗的演练场。

sentences.en: It's outside the city.
sentences.zh: 它在城外。

sentences.en: And Miltiades is just one of 10 generals?
sentences.zh: 米太亚得只是十位将军之一吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's a board of 10 generals.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个由十人组成的将军委员会。

sentences.en: He's not the supreme commander.
sentences.zh: 他不是最高统帅。

sentences.en: The supreme commander is a guy called Callimachus, the war archon.
sentences.zh: 最高统帅是一个叫卡利马科斯的人，他是战争执政官。

sentences.en: The war archon.
sentences.zh: 战争执政官。

sentences.en: So they've all been elected by public vote.
sentences.zh: 他们都是通过公众投票选出来的。

sentences.en: The war archon, Callimachus, he's an overall command.
sentences.zh: 战争执政官卡利马科斯拥有最高指挥权。

sentences.en: But the generals, you have 10 of them for each of the kind of the various tribes that the democracy has set up.
sentences.zh: 但将军们，民主制设立的各个部落每个都有十位将军。

sentences.en: So Miltiades is commander of his tribe.
sentences.zh: 所以米太亚得是他所在部落的指挥官。

sentences.en: And each of these 10 commanders take it in turn to be Callimachus's subordinate.
sentences.zh: 这十位指挥官轮流担任卡利马科斯的下属。

sentences.en: So to have the kind of overall control.
sentences.zh: 从而拥有某种整体控制权。

sentences.en: And how many men are we talking about?
sentences.zh: 我们说的是多少人？

sentences.en: Probably around 10,000 men.
sentences.zh: 大约一万人左右。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And they head off and they have slaves to carry their armor.
sentences.zh: 他们出发了，有奴隶帮他们携带盔甲。

sentences.en: They have pack animals to carry their rations.
sentences.zh: 他们有驮畜来携带口粮。

sentences.en: And they take one of the two roads that leads from Athens to Marathon and probably the coastal road.
sentences.zh: 他们选择了从雅典到马拉松的两条路之一，很可能是沿海公路。

sentences.en: Because although it's 26 miles against 22 miles, which is the other road, the other road takes you up into the mountains.
sentences.zh: 因为虽然这条路有26英里，而另一条路只有22英里，但另一条路会把你带进山区。

sentences.en: So you're much more kind of vulnerable there.
sentences.zh: 所以你在那里会更容易受到攻击。

sentences.en: And also it would leave the coastal road open to the cavalry.
sentences.zh: 而且这也会让沿海公路对骑兵敞开。

sentences.en: So I'm fairly confident that they take the coastal road.
sentences.zh: 所以我相当肯定他们走的是沿海公路。

sentences.en: And they march at tremendous speed.
sentences.zh: 他们以惊人的速度行军。

sentences.en: And Athenians going at a tremendous speed is going to be a theme of this episode.
sentences.zh: 而雅典人以惊人的速度行进将是这一集的主题。

sentences.en: And they arrive at the crest of the hill that overlooks Marathon from the south.
sentences.zh: 他们抵达了从南面俯瞰马拉松的山脊。

sentences.en: And you mentioned Order of the Rings.
sentences.zh: 你提到了《指环王》。

sentences.en: This is kind of like the riders of Rowan gazing down at the battlefield of Pelennor Fields.
sentences.zh: 这就像洛汗骑兵俯瞰帕兰诺平原战场一样。

sentences.en: Because what they see, I mean, is terrifying.
sentences.zh: 因为他们所看到的，我的意思是，太可怕了。

sentences.en: The bay is black with ships.
sentences.zh: 海湾里黑压压的全是船只。

sentences.en: They can see these ships, you know, arms and provisions and horses being unloaded across this kind of great seaweed matted beach.
sentences.zh: 他们能看到这些船，你知道，武器、补给和马匹正从这片长满海藻的巨大海滩上卸下。

sentences.en: And presumably there are already Persian outriders kind of raising dust across the plain, reconnoitering the limits of the plain.
sentences.zh: 想必已经有波斯斥候在平原上扬起尘土，侦察平原的边界了。

sentences.en: And it's these horsemen who most terrify the Athenians because they know that they will be very, very vulnerable to attack by horsemen.
sentences.zh: 正是这些骑兵让雅典人感到最恐惧，因为他们知道自己非常容易受到骑兵的攻击。

sentences.en: And they are kind of lumbering, heavy infantry.
sentences.zh: 他们是那种笨重的重装步兵。

sentences.en: They would be sitting ducks if they were caught in the open by the horse.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在开阔地被骑兵抓住，就会成为活靶子。

sentences.en: Just a question.
sentences.zh: 问个问题。

sentences.en: Athenians have no horsemen at all.
sentences.zh: 雅典人根本没有骑兵吗？

sentences.en: No, not really.
sentences.zh: 没有，真的没有。

sentences.en: Because their force and their power comes from infantry.
sentences.zh: 因为他们的力量和权力来自步兵。

sentences.en: So even those who are very wealthy will generally fight on foot.
sentences.zh: 所以即使是非常富有的人通常也会步行作战。

sentences.en: And that kind of determines their strategy.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上决定了他们的战略。

sentences.en: Basically, they have to hold their defensive position.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们必须守住防御阵地。

sentences.en: They cannot afford to go down into the plain because otherwise it really would be curtains.
sentences.zh: 他们负担不起进入平原的代价，否则就真的完了。

sentences.en: But actually, they don't need to leave the heights because they've arrived in time to block any Persian advance on Athens.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他们不需要离开高地，因为他们及时赶到，封锁了波斯人向雅典推进的任何路线。

sentences.en: And so to that extent, Mild Hyades' plan has worked.
sentences.zh: 从这个程度上说，米太亚得的计划奏效了。

sentences.en: And there's a shrine to Heracles on the heights, which has a kind of a grove in front of it, which provides a degree of screening.
sentences.zh: 高地上有一座赫拉克勒斯神庙，前面有一片树林，提供了一定程度的掩护。

sentences.en: And so they fortify the Temple of Heracles.
sentences.zh: 于是他们加固了赫拉克勒斯神庙。

sentences.en: They set up their lines along the road.
sentences.zh: 他们在路边布防。

sentences.en: And they are sufficiently strong there, I think, that it is going to be very, very difficult for the Persians to make a full frontal attack.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们在那里足够强大，波斯人很难进行全面的正面进攻。

sentences.en: So there is now a kind of stalemate.
sentences.zh: 所以现在陷入了某种僵局。

sentences.en: And this is promising for the Athenians because it means that there might be time now for reinforcements to arrive.
sentences.zh: 这对雅典人来说很有希望，因为这意味着现在可能有时间等待援军到达。

sentences.en: The Athenians are not generally very popular.
sentences.zh: 雅典人通常不太受欢迎。

sentences.en: They're a big city.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个大城市。

sentences.en: They throw their weight around.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢仗势欺人。

sentences.en: They're endlessly going on about how brilliant they are with their liberty and everything.
sentences.zh: 他们没完没了地吹嘘自己的自由和一切有多么辉煌。

sentences.en: Kind of other cities find them annoying.
sentences.zh: 其他城市觉得他们很烦人。

sentences.en: But they do have one city which is completely committed to the Athenian cause.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实有一个完全致力于雅典事业的城市。

sentences.en: The city loves Athens.
sentences.zh: 那个城市热爱雅典。

sentences.en: And this is a city called Plataea, a very small city, which lies to the northwest of Athens in the sphere of influence of Thebes,
sentences.zh: 这就是普拉提亚，一个非常小的城市，位于雅典西北部，处于底比斯的势力范围内，

sentences.en: which has always been the Athenians' traditional enemy.
sentences.zh: 而底比斯一直是雅典人的传统敌人。

sentences.en: Although Hippias, the old Tyrannos, had had had quite good relations with the Thebans.
sentences.zh: 尽管老僭主希庇亚斯与底比斯人关系相当不错。

sentences.en: But when he'd been expelled, the Athenians had gone back to their old ways and kind of gone to war with the Thebans.
sentences.zh: 但当他被驱逐后，雅典人又回到了老路上，与底比斯人开战了。

sentences.en: And as a democracy, Athens had become Plataea's big brother because Plataea is always being kind of menaced by the Thebans.
sentences.zh: 作为民主国家，雅典成了普拉提亚的老大哥，因为普拉提亚总是受到底比斯人的威胁。

sentences.en: And so the Athenians step in and say, well, yeah, we'll protect you.
sentences.zh: 所以雅典人介入并说，好吧，我们会保护你们。

sentences.en: We'll look after you.
sentences.zh: 我们会照顾你们。

sentences.en: And now it's the Athenians' hour of need.
sentences.zh: 现在是雅典人危难的时刻。

sentences.en: And so the Plataeans remember the debt.
sentences.zh: 所以普拉提亚人记住了这份恩情。

sentences.en: And even though they're a very small city, they can only raise about 800 men.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们是一个非常小的城市，只能召集大约800人。

sentences.en: They send all those 800 men to bolster the Athenian army.
sentences.zh: 他们派出了这全部800人来加强雅典军队。

sentences.en: And it's not a huge contingent.
sentences.zh: 这不是一支庞大的队伍。

sentences.en: But obviously, their arrival touches every Athenian heart.
sentences.zh: 但显然，他们的到来触动了每一位雅典人的心。

sentences.en: I mean, it's an incredibly moving scene when they arrive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们到达时是一个极其感人的场景。

sentences.en: This is the little ships at Dunkirk moment.
sentences.zh: 这就是敦刻尔克小船时刻。

sentences.en: And the Athenians will never forget.
sentences.zh: 雅典人永远不会忘记。

sentences.en: They will never forget this moment.
sentences.zh: 他们永远不会忘记这一刻。

sentences.en: But there are, of course, two cities that have two major cities that have stood against the Persians.
sentences.zh: 当然，有两个城市，两个主要城市一直站在波斯人的对立面。

sentences.en: So one is Athens and the other is Sparta.
sentences.zh: 一个是雅典，另一个是斯巴达。

sentences.en: And the Athenians must be thinking, are the Spartans going to show up?
sentences.zh: 雅典人一定在想，斯巴达人会来吗？

sentences.en: We need the Spartans to join us.
sentences.zh: 我们需要斯巴达人加入我们。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the Spartans, of course, are the most formidable military power in Greece.
sentences.zh: 当然，斯巴达人是希腊最强大的军事力量。

sentences.en: So to have the Spartans turn up would really tilt the balance in favor of the Athenians, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，如果斯巴达人出现，真的会使天平向雅典人倾斜。

sentences.en: And because of that, even as the mass of the Athenian army is heading towards Marathon from Athens,
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，即使当雅典军队的主力正从雅典向马拉松进发时，

sentences.en: there is one Athenian who is heading in the opposite direction and taking the road that will lead him to the Isthmus of Corinth
sentences.zh: 有一位雅典人正朝着相反的方向前进，走上了通往科林斯地峡的道路，

sentences.en: and then down through the Peloponnese towards Sparta.
sentences.zh: 然后穿过伯罗奔尼撒半岛前往斯巴达。

sentences.en: And this is a man called Pheidippides.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫菲迪皮德斯。

sentences.en: And he is celebrated as the greatest runner in the whole of Athens.
sentences.zh: 他被誉为整个雅典最伟大的跑步者。

sentences.en: And he covers the 140 miles that separate Athens from Sparta in two days.
sentences.zh: 他在两天内跑完了雅典到斯巴达之间140英里的路程。

sentences.en: So an incredible feat.
sentences.zh: 真是不可思议的壮举。

sentences.en: And on the second evening of this epic run, he arrives in the wall-less plains of Sparta.
sentences.zh: 在这场史诗般奔跑的第二个傍晚，他抵达了没有城墙的斯巴达平原。

sentences.en: And he brings his news.
sentences.zh: 他带来了消息。

sentences.en: The Persians have landed at Marathon.
sentences.zh: 波斯人已经在马拉松登陆了。

sentences.en: And the Athenians have every hope that the Spartans will come.
sentences.zh: 雅典人对斯巴达人会来抱有全部希望。

sentences.en: They are a very proud military power.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个非常自豪的军事强国。

sentences.en: However, their prestige is at stake if they don't come to support the Athenians in their hour of need, I think.
sentences.zh: 然而，我认为如果他们不在雅典人危难时刻前来支援，他们的声望就会受到威胁。

sentences.en: They have chucked Dares' messengers down a well and told them to get earth and water from there.
sentences.zh: 他们曾把大流士的使者扔进井里，告诉他们去那里取土和水。

sentences.en: You know, this is Sparta and all of that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是斯巴达，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they've promised that they will come.
sentences.zh: 他们承诺过会来。

sentences.en: And, you know, the Spartans don't give their word lightly.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，斯巴达人不会轻易许诺。

sentences.en: And so Pheidippides arrives.
sentences.zh: 于是菲迪皮德斯到了。

sentences.en: He's obviously, I'm imagining, very much out of breath.
sentences.zh: 我想他显然已经气喘吁吁了。

sentences.en: But he pants it out.
sentences.zh: 但他喘着气说出了请求。

sentences.en: Men of Sparta, the Athenians beg you for assistance.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人，雅典人恳求你们的援助。

sentences.en: Do not, by looking the other way, allow the most ancient city in Greece to fall into bondage.
sentences.zh: 不要因为袖手旁观，而让希腊最古老的城市陷入奴役。

sentences.en: And the clutches of barbarians.
sentences.zh: 落入野蛮人的魔掌。

sentences.en: Oh, but the timing is terrible because the Spartans are celebrating a great feaSt.
sentences.zh: 哦，但时机太糟糕了，因为斯巴达人正在庆祝一个盛大的节日。

sentences.en: This is the feast of the Carnea.
sentences.zh: 这就是卡尔内亚节。

sentences.en: It's sacred to Apollo and it is one of their holiest festivals.
sentences.zh: 它献给阿波罗，是他们最神圣的节日之一。

sentences.en: And it's a time of truce.
sentences.zh: 这是一个休战时期。

sentences.en: The Spartans just cannot fight during the festival of the Carnea.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人在卡尔内亚节期间绝对不能打仗。

sentences.en: Well, even if the persons are attacking, they still can't, they've got important, you know, religious duties and they can't know.
sentences.zh: 好吧，即使波斯人正在进攻，他们仍然不能，他们有重要的宗教职责，他们不能……

sentences.en: And it's often been assumed that this is, you know, that they're scamming it, that they don't really want to come, that they're happy.
sentences.zh: 人们经常认为这是，你知道，他们在找借口，他们其实不想来，他们很高兴。

sentences.en: I don't think this is true at all.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是真的。

sentences.en: The Spartans are, by our lights, madly superstitious.
sentences.zh: 在我们看来，斯巴达人简直迷信得不可理喻。

sentences.en: So, we did an episode on the Battle of Thermopylae that takes place 10 years after Marathon.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们做了一期关于马拉松战役十年后发生的温泉关战役的节目。

sentences.en: And there's all kinds of shenanigans there because the Spartans can't send troops to Thermopylae because the Festival of Olympia, the Olympic Games is on.
sentences.zh: 当时发生了很多变故，因为斯巴达人无法派兵前往温泉关，正赶上奥林匹亚节，也就是奥林匹克运动会期间。

sentences.en: And I think it's exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 我觉得情况完全一样。

sentences.en: They do, if they're going to go and fight the Persians, they don't want to annoy Apollo before they do it.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是这样，如果他们要去和波斯人作战，他们不想在行动前惹怒阿波罗。

sentences.en: I mean, that's mad.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: So, I think that their inability to leave is entirely genuine.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为他们无法离开是完全真实的。

sentences.en: Their religious scruples are not just kind of invented.
sentences.zh: 他们的宗教顾虑并非凭空捏造。

sentences.en: And so, they say to Pheidippides, we're really sorry.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们对斐里庇底斯说，我们真的很抱歉。

sentences.en: We can't leave for another week.
sentences.zh: 我们一周内无法离开。

sentences.en: And then it will probably take us three or four days to get to Marathon.
sentences.zh: 而且我们可能需要三四天才能到达马拉松。

sentences.en: So, that's 10 days in all.
sentences.zh: 所以，总共需要10天。

sentences.en: We're really sorry.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很抱歉。

sentences.en: But we will be with you in 10 days.
sentences.zh: 但我们会在10天内赶到。

sentences.en: So, Pheidippides is gutted by this.
sentences.zh: 所以，斐里庇底斯对此感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: But I guess it's not, you know, a complete disaster.
sentences.zh: 但我猜这也不是什么彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: At least if the Athenians can hold their position, then the Spartans may arrive.
sentences.zh: 至少如果雅典人能守住阵地，斯巴达人或许能赶到。

sentences.en: He heads out of Sparta.
sentences.zh: 他离开了斯巴达。

sentences.en: He takes the mountain road that leads up through the highlands of central Peloponnese.
sentences.zh: 他走的是穿过伯罗奔尼撒半岛中部高地的山路。

sentences.en: And while he's up in the highlands, he meets someone who promises that he will be at Marathon with the Athenians come what may.
sentences.zh: 当他在高地上时，他遇见了一个人，那人承诺无论如何都会在马拉松与雅典人并肩作战。

sentences.en: And this is a very unexpected apparition.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常出人意料的幻象。

sentences.en: It's a figure with the legs of a goat, two curling horns, and an absolutely enormous phallus.
sentences.zh: 那是一个长着山羊腿、一对弯曲的角，以及一个硕大无比的生殖器的形象。

sentences.en: And this is the god Pan.
sentences.zh: 这就是神潘。

sentences.en: And he is a god who's so notorious for ambushing wayfarers like Pheidippides, kind of lonely up in the mountain heights and filling them with terror,
sentences.zh: 他是一位以伏击像斐里庇底斯这样在山间孤独行走的旅人并让他们充满恐惧而闻名的神，

sentences.en: that that sense of terror has its own name in Greek, which derives from Pan.
sentences.zh: 以至于那种恐惧感在希腊语中有一个专门的词，源自潘的名字。

sentences.en: And the word is panikon, from which we get our English word panic.
sentences.zh: 这个词是panikon，也就是我们英语中“恐慌”（panic）一词的来源。

sentences.en: And so that gives you a sense of what Pan may be offering to bring to the table when and if a battle is fought at Marathon.
sentences.zh: 这让你明白如果马拉松战役打响，潘可能会带来什么。

sentences.en: Because he tells Pheidippides that he has a message for the Athenians.
sentences.zh: 因为他告诉斐里庇底斯，他有一条给雅典人的口信。

sentences.en: Why, when I am so fond of you, do you rebuff me?
sentences.zh: 为什么我如此喜欢你们，你们却要拒绝我？

sentences.en: I have done you many favors in the past and will do so again in the future.
sentences.zh: 我过去曾帮过你们很多忙，将来也会继续这样做。

sentences.en: So essentially, Pan is saying, if you offer me the respect that I am due, you know, you give me sacrifices, celebrate me, give me festivals and things.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，潘是在说，如果你们给予我应有的尊重，比如向我献祭，赞美我，为我举办节日等等。

sentences.en: Then I will be at Marathon with you, and I will fill the Persians with a sense of panic.
sentences.zh: 那么我就会在马拉松与你们同在，我会让波斯人陷入恐慌。

sentences.en: And so Pheidippides banks this, he carries on on his way, he gets to Marathon, and he passes on the message from Pan, and he passes on the message from the Spartans.
sentences.zh: 斐里庇底斯记下了这些，继续赶路，他到达了马拉松，传达了潘的口信，也传达了斯巴达人的口信。

sentences.en: They're going to be there in 10 days' time.
sentences.zh: 他们会在10天后到达。

sentences.en: There's good news and bad news.
sentences.zh: 有好消息也有坏消息。

sentences.en: The Spartans are going to be a bit delayed.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人会迟到一点。

sentences.en: On the other hand...
sentences.zh: 另一方面……

sentences.en: I think that the news of the Spartans, I mean, it's a bit of a downer, but it's not a complete downer, because they can afford to hold their positions and wait.
sentences.zh: 我认为斯巴达人的消息，虽然有点令人沮丧，但并不是彻底的打击，因为他们有能力守住阵地并等待。

sentences.en: It is a problem for the Persians, and the Persians have a very proficient espionage system.
sentences.zh: 这对波斯人来说是个问题，而且波斯人有一套非常高效的间谍系统。

sentences.en: So it's almost certain that they would know the likely date of the Spartan arrival pretty soon after the arrival of Pheidippides in the Athenian camp.
sentences.zh: 所以几乎可以肯定，在斐里庇底斯到达雅典军营后不久，他们就会知道斯巴达人可能到达的日期。

sentences.en: And their situation is a tricky one.
sentences.zh: 他们的处境很棘手。

sentences.en: Because on the one hand, they can't really afford to attack the Athenians' defensive position.
sentences.zh: 因为一方面，他们真的无法承受攻击雅典人的防御阵地。

sentences.en: It's too big an ask.
sentences.zh: 那要求太高了。

sentences.en: On the other hand, you know, they need to get everything done and dusted before the Spartans arrive.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，他们需要在斯巴达人到达之前完成一切。

sentences.en: So they have this kind of 10-day window.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有这样一个10天的窗口期。

sentences.en: So what are they going to do?
sentences.zh: 那么他们会怎么做呢？

sentences.en: Now, Miltiades is very familiar with their way of making war.
sentences.zh: 米太亚得非常熟悉他们的作战方式。

sentences.en: And I think he has a very shrewd idea what the Persians will end up doing.
sentences.zh: 我想他非常敏锐地预料到了波斯人最终会做什么。

sentences.en: And it's probably, you know, right from the beginning, what he's been expecting they are going to do.
sentences.zh: 而且这很可能就是他从一开始就预料到他们会做的事情。

sentences.en: But only time will tell if he is right.
sentences.zh: 但只有时间能证明他是否正确。

sentences.en: So I'm not going to say what the Persians do, but we will see whether Miltiades is right or not.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会说波斯人做了什么，但我们会看到米太亚得是否正确。

sentences.en: So a day passes, and then another, and then another.
sentences.zh: 一天过去了，又一天，再一天。

sentences.en: And in time, there are four days left until the Spartans are due to arrive.
sentences.zh: 时间流逝，距离斯巴达人预定到达的时间还剩四天。

sentences.en: And this deadlock holds the Persians down in the plain.
sentences.zh: 这种僵局将波斯人困在平原上。

sentences.en: The Athenians blocking their exit from the plain on this crucial road.
sentences.zh: 雅典人在这条关键道路上阻断了他们离开平原的出口。

sentences.en: And four days before the Spartans are due to arrive, the sun sets behind the mountains that look on marathon.
sentences.zh: 在斯巴达人预定到达的前四天，太阳落在了俯瞰马拉松的山峦之后。

sentences.en: And the moon rises silver in the sky.
sentences.zh: 月亮在天空中升起，银光闪烁。

sentences.en: And in distant Sparta, the carnea is now over.
sentences.zh: 在遥远的斯巴达，卡尔内亚节现在结束了。

sentences.en: The Spartans are mustering.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人正在集结。

sentences.en: They are getting ready to march.
sentences.zh: 他们准备出发了。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, in the Persian camp, as dusk is succeeded by the darkness of night,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在波斯军营里，随着黄昏被黑夜取代，

sentences.en: the Athenians hear this incredible commotion, and it's the sound of thousands of pairs of tramping feet moving towards the Athenian positions across the plain.
sentences.zh: 雅典人听到了巨大的骚动，那是成千上万双脚步声在平原上向雅典阵地移动的声音。

sentences.en: And so the Athenians wonder what's going on.
sentences.zh: 雅典人想知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: Is this a full frontal assault, or is it a diversion, or what's happening?
sentences.zh: 这是正面强攻，还是佯攻，或者发生了什么？

sentences.en: And the answer to that question arrives very soon.
sentences.zh: 这个问题的答案很快就揭晓了。

sentences.en: And this is courtesy of Ionian conscripts who were with the Persian expedition and who've been recruited almost certainly by Miltiades,
sentences.zh: 这要归功于随波斯远征军而来的爱奥尼亚应征士兵，他们几乎可以肯定是米太亚得招募的，

sentences.en: who would have had all kinds of contacts with the Ionians, to serve the Athenians as spies.
sentences.zh: 米太亚得与爱奥尼亚人有着各种联系，他们被招募来为雅典人充当间谍。

sentences.en: And they bring news so momentous that it is immediately brought to the Athenian high command.
sentences.zh: 他们带来的消息极其重大，以至于立即被送到了雅典最高指挥部。

sentences.en: So that is Calimachus, who is the war archon, the guy in overall command.
sentences.zh: 那就是卡利马科斯，他是战时执政官，负责全面指挥。

sentences.en: Miltiades, the man who knows more about the Persian way of war than anyone else in Athens, and his fellow nine generals on the board of generals.
sentences.zh: 米太亚得，这个比雅典任何人都更了解波斯作战方式的人，以及他在将军委员会中的其他九位同僚。

sentences.en: And here is the news that the Ionians have brought.
sentences.zh: 这就是爱奥尼亚人带来的消息。

sentences.en: The tramping that the Athenians can hear is that of a holding force.
sentences.zh: 雅典人听到的脚步声是一支牵制部队发出的。

sentences.en: It is not, it seems, an assault.
sentences.zh: 看来这并不是进攻。

sentences.en: It has been sent to distract them.
sentences.zh: 它是被派来分散他们注意力的。

sentences.en: And to distract them from what?
sentences.zh: 分散他们对什么的注意力？

sentences.en: Well, the fact that the Persian task force is being divided in two.
sentences.zh: 好吧，波斯特遣部队正在一分为二。

sentences.en: And why has the Persian task force been divided in two?
sentences.zh: 为什么波斯特遣部队要一分为二？

sentences.en: Because clearly, Datis has decided that with the Spartan arrival now imminent, he needs to trap the Athenians, if he possibly can, in a pincer movement.
sentences.zh: 因为很明显，达提斯认为随着斯巴达人的即将到来，他必须尽可能地用钳形攻势困住雅典人。

sentences.en: And so that means that he wants to send a portion of his forces around the back in transport ships down the Athenian coast to see if they can find an alternative landing spot.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他想派出一部分兵力，乘坐运输船绕到后方，沿着雅典海岸航行，看看能否找到另一个登陆点。

sentences.en: And then to march up the road towards the Athenians and kind of catch them in this pincer force.
sentences.zh: 然后沿路向雅典人进军，用这种钳形攻势困住他们。

sentences.en: And which part of his force is he sending to do this?
sentences.zh: 他派出了哪部分兵力来做这件事？

sentences.en: And this is the crucial detail.
sentences.zh: 这是关键细节。

sentences.en: And it is given to the Athenian high command by the Ionian spies.
sentences.zh: 这是爱奥尼亚间谍提供给雅典最高指挥部的。

sentences.en: It's the horsemen.
sentences.zh: 是骑兵。

sentences.en: So this famous phrase that the Ionians deliver, the cavalry have left.
sentences.zh: 所以爱奥尼亚人传达了那句名言：骑兵已经离开了。

sentences.en: They're leaving the plain.
sentences.zh: 他们正在离开平原。

sentences.en: And here, if the Athenians can only dare to seize it, is their big, big opportunity.
sentences.zh: 如果雅典人敢于抓住这个机会，这就是他们千载难逢的大好时机。

sentences.en: It is the chance to take on the Persians, while the most lethal part of their task force, their cavalry, are absent from the field of battle.
sentences.zh: 这是一个在波斯特遣部队中最致命的部分——骑兵——缺席战场时，与波斯人交战的机会。

sentences.en: But of course, to do that will require the Athenians to leave their defensive positions and advance down into the plain.
sentences.zh: 但当然，要做到这一点，雅典人必须离开防御阵地，推进到平原上。

sentences.en: And so the huge question is, will the Athenians dare to seize this opportunity?
sentences.zh: 所以最大的问题是，雅典人敢于抓住这个机会吗？

sentences.en: What an unbelievable cliffhanger.
sentences.zh: 真是令人难以置信的悬念。

sentences.en: Will the Athenians seize the moment?
sentences.zh: 雅典人会抓住时机吗？

sentences.en: Find out after the break.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，揭晓答案。

sentences.en: On a rainy bridge over an Amsterdam canal, bearded Dutchmen in black capes and white ruffs shake hands on deals that will change the world.
sentences.zh: 在阿姆斯特丹运河上一座阴雨绵绵的桥上，留着胡须、身披黑斗篷、戴着白色褶皱领的荷兰人握手达成协议，这些协议将改变世界。

sentences.en: This is the early 1600s.
sentences.zh: 那是17世纪初。

sentences.en: And these men have created a company that in today's money is so wealthy that at its peak, it's more than twice the value of Apple and NVIDIA combined.
sentences.zh: 这些人创建了一家公司，按今天的货币计算，它在鼎盛时期的财富是苹果和英伟达总和的两倍多。

sentences.en: Hello, Restless History listeners.
sentences.zh: 你好，Restless History的听众们。

sentences.en: I'm William de Rimpel.
sentences.zh: 我是威廉·德·林佩尔。

sentences.en: And I'm Anita Arnand.
sentences.zh: 我是安妮塔·阿南德。

sentences.en: And we are the hosts of a fellow goalhanger history podcast called Empire.
sentences.zh: 我们是Goalhanger旗下历史播客《帝国》的主持人。

sentences.en: On Empire this week, we are exploring the extraordinary story of the Dutch East India Company.
sentences.zh: 本周在《帝国》节目中，我们将探索荷兰东印度公司的非凡故事。

sentences.en: It's a story of the very first corporate espionage, the colonisation of Indonesia and a swap that leads to the creation of New York City.

sentences.en: Dawn has not yet broken on one of the most fateful days, not merely in Greek history, but perhaps in the history of the world.
sentences.zh: 黎明尚未破晓，这不仅是希腊历史上，或许也是世界历史上最决定性的日子之一。

sentences.en: And we find ourselves in the tent of the war archon, Callimachus, where he and his captains are debating what to do.
sentences.zh: 我们发现自己身处战时执政官卡利马科斯的帐篷里，他和他的队长们正在争论该怎么做。

sentences.en: So Tom, tell us about who's on which side in this debate.
sentences.zh: 那么汤姆，告诉我们这场辩论中双方都有谁。

sentences.en: Okay, on one side is Miltiades, and he has one particular advantage in making his case, which is that it is his turn to command the Athenians on this day of days.
sentences.zh: 好的，一边是米太亚得，他在陈述观点时有一个特殊的优势，那就是在这一天，轮到他指挥雅典人了。

sentences.en: So that's an incredible slice of luck for him.
sentences.zh: 所以对他来说，这真是天大的运气。

sentences.en: He is pushing for the Athenians to advance from their defensive positions down into the plain and attack the Asiatic hordes, which are swarming down there.
sentences.zh: 他正在推动雅典人从防御阵地推进到平原，攻击在那里蜂拥而至的亚洲部落。

sentences.en: Because he can see with this, you know, the clarity of the seasoned enemy of the Persians that he is, that there is this precious but fleeting opportunity.
sentences.zh: 因为他以那种久经沙场的波斯敌人的敏锐眼光可以看到，这是一个宝贵但转瞬即逝的机会。

sentences.en: And in fact, I think that this is what he had been expecting and waiting for.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为这正是他一直期待和等待的。

sentences.en: This is what he had been expecting the Persians would be forced to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是他一直预料波斯人会被迫做的事情。

sentences.en: And he's recognized it as the one chance the Athenians have for victory.
sentences.zh: 他将其视为雅典人获胜的唯一机会。

sentences.en: So his understanding of what Datis is up to, I think, is as follows.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他对达提斯意图的理解如下。

sentences.en: Datis does not want to wait for the Spartans to arrive, but he can't force the road that leads to Athens.
sentences.zh: 达提斯不想等待斯巴达人到来，但他无法强行通过通往雅典的道路。

sentences.en: And so his only real option then is to split his forces by loading some of them into transport ships and sending them down the coastline.
sentences.zh: 所以他唯一真正的选择就是将部队一分为二，将其中一部分装上运输船，沿着海岸线南下。

sentences.en: And if he's going to do that, then it makes sense to send his cavalry because they can then advance back up the road as fast as possible.
sentences.zh: 如果他真的要这么做，那么派走骑兵就是合情合理的，因为这样他们就能以最快的速度沿原路返回。

sentences.en: And if the intelligence that has been brought to the Athenians by their spies in the Persian camp is accurate, then this is exactly what is happening.
sentences.zh: 如果雅典人从波斯军营的间谍那里得到的情报准确无误，那么现在发生的正是这种情况。

sentences.en: This Persian holding force has been sent to distract the Athenians, while far in the rear, the cavalry are being clandestinely loaded onto the transport ships and starting to sail
sentences.zh: 这支波斯牵制部队被派来分散雅典人的注意力，而在后方远处，骑兵正被秘密地装上运输船，并开始启航

sentences.en: away down the Attic coaSt.
sentences.zh: 沿着阿提卡海岸驶离。

sentences.en: So the Athenians will never have a better chance of victory.
sentences.zh: 所以雅典人再也不会有比这更好的获胜机会了。

sentences.en: The invader's army is divided and the cavalry have temporarily vacated the field.
sentences.zh: 入侵者的军队被分开了，骑兵也暂时离开了战场。

sentences.en: But this window of opportunity is going to close very faSt.
sentences.zh: 但这个机会窗口很快就会关闭。

sentences.en: They have to seize their opportunity as soon as they possibly can.
sentences.zh: 他们必须尽快抓住这个机会。

sentences.en: And four of Miltiades' fellow generals are convinced by this, but five are appalled by it.
sentences.zh: 米太亚得的同僚将军中有四人被说服了，但有五人对此感到震惊。

sentences.en: And I think it's important to emphasize just how terrifying the suggestion that Miltiades is
sentences.zh: 我认为有必要强调一下米太亚得提出的建议有多么可怕，

sentences.en: making, that they are being asked to attack the Persians on open ground, which the Athenians
sentences.zh: 他们被要求在开阔地带攻击波斯人，而雅典人

sentences.en: have always known is the one place you don't attack the Persians, without archers, without cavalry, still outnumbered, even if the cavalry has gone.
sentences.zh: 一直都知道那是绝对不能攻击波斯人的地方，而且他们没有弓箭手，没有骑兵，人数依然处于劣势，即便骑兵已经离开。

sentences.en: And just to reiterate, no Greek army has ever defeated the Persians in open combat.
sentences.zh: 再次重申，此前没有任何希腊军队在正面交锋中击败过波斯人。

sentences.en: So you can see why there is opposition to Miltiades' plan.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以理解为什么米太亚得的计划会遭到反对。

sentences.en: I mean, so much hangs in the balance.
sentences.zh: 我是说，胜负在此一举。

sentences.en: And they're evenly divided, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 他们的意见势均力敌，不是吗？

sentences.en: So the casting vote will go to the war archon Callimachus.
sentences.zh: 所以决定性的一票将由军事执政官卡利马科斯投出。

sentences.en: And which way will he side?
sentences.zh: 他会站在哪一边呢？

sentences.en: He sides with Miltiades.
sentences.zh: 他站在了米太亚得这一边。

sentences.en: Let's go for it.
sentences.zh: 我们上吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: The order is given.
sentences.zh: 命令下达了。

sentences.en: Battle is going to be joined at dawn.
sentences.zh: 战斗将在黎明时分打响。

sentences.en: Messengers go throughout the camp.
sentences.zh: 信使们穿梭于军营之中。

sentences.en: The Athenians start to wake up and they are told the news that they are going to descend into the plain and there will be a battle for the future of Athens fought that day.
sentences.zh: 雅典人开始醒来，他们接到消息说，他们将下到平原，在那一天为雅典的未来进行一场战斗。

sentences.en: So they get up, they have their breakfast and then slaves bring them their equipment, a hoplite.
sentences.zh: 于是他们起床，吃过早餐，然后奴隶们把装备带给他们，重装步兵。

sentences.en: So their shields, their helmets, their spears.
sentences.zh: 也就是他们的盾牌、头盔和长矛。

sentences.en: And hoplite is the word that gives us the name for a Greek heavy infantryman, hoplite.
sentences.zh: “重装步兵”（hoplite）这个词就是我们现在所说的希腊重装步兵的名称来源。

sentences.en: And the bare minimum that these hoplites would have is a helmet, a shield, a spear, a sword.
sentences.zh: 这些重装步兵最基本的装备是头盔、盾牌、长矛和剑。

sentences.en: And some of the Plataeans don't even have helmets.
sentences.zh: 有些普拉提亚人甚至没有头盔。

sentences.en: They just have leather caps, which are called dog skins.
sentences.zh: 他们只有皮帽，被称为“狗皮帽”。

sentences.en: So not everybody is kind of sheathed in bronze.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是每个人都全身披挂青铜。

sentences.en: But most Athenians, they do have corslets.
sentences.zh: 但大多数雅典人确实有胸甲。

sentences.en: Some of these corslets are of bronze.
sentences.zh: 有些胸甲是青铜制的。

sentences.en: Some are made of layers of cloth stuck onto a kind of leather jerkin.
sentences.zh: 有些是用布层粘在一种皮背心上制成的。

sentences.en: Some of these leather jerkins would have bronze scales sewn into them.
sentences.zh: 有些皮背心上会缝入青铜鳞片。

sentences.en: And also you would put bronze greaves on your shins to protect your legs.
sentences.zh: 此外，你还要在小腿上戴上青铜护胫来保护双腿。

sentences.en: And so there's no uniformity in terms of kit.
sentences.zh: 所以装备并没有统一标准。

sentences.en: And the total weight is kind of estimated between 30, 70 pounds.
sentences.zh: 总重量估计在30到70磅之间。

sentences.en: I mean, that's quite a lot.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这相当重。

sentences.en: And the most heavily armored of all, those who can afford the most armor.
sentences.zh: 而装备最精良的，是那些买得起最多盔甲的人。

sentences.en: I mean, they are kind of fearsome automata of bronze.
sentences.zh: 他们简直就是可怕的青铜自动机。

sentences.en: I mean, they are really, really very heavily clad.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们穿得真的非常非常厚重。

sentences.en: And by dawn, so as the sun is rising to the east over the Aegean, the hoplites are ready for battle.
sentences.zh: 到了黎明，当太阳从爱琴海东面升起时，重装步兵们已经准备好战斗了。

sentences.en: If they've got breastplates, they've put them on.
sentences.zh: 如果有胸甲，他们已经穿上了。

sentences.en: If they've got greaves, they've strapped them on.
sentences.zh: 如果有护胫，他们已经绑好了。

sentences.en: They've got their shields.
sentences.zh: 他们拿好了盾牌。

sentences.en: They've got their spears in their hands.
sentences.zh: 他们手里握着长矛。

sentences.en: They've got their helmets propped up on the back of their heads.
sentences.zh: 他们把头盔推到了脑后。

sentences.en: And then, of course, they have to be arrayed for battle.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们还得列阵作战。

sentences.en: And the customary Athenian practice is to line up a phalanx, the great kind of porcubine of spears that is formed by lines and lines of Greek infantrymen equipped with spears.
sentences.zh: 雅典人的惯例是排成方阵，那是由一排排装备长矛的希腊步兵组成的巨大的“长矛豪猪”。

sentences.en: Normally, an Athenian phalanx consists of eight lines.
sentences.zh: 通常，一个雅典方阵由八排组成。

sentences.en: But Miltiades, he can see down into the plain now.
sentences.zh: 但米太亚得现在可以俯瞰平原。

sentences.en: There's a kind of grey light as the sun starts to rise.
sentences.zh: 随着太阳开始升起，光线呈现出一种灰色。

sentences.en: And he can see that the Persian lines, because they outnumber the Athenians so strongly, is much longer than if the Athenian phalanx was eight lines deep.
sentences.zh: 他可以看到波斯人的阵线，因为他们的人数远超雅典人，所以比八排深的雅典方阵要长得多。

sentences.en: And so he extends the Athenian line to match the Persian line.
sentences.zh: 于是他拉长了雅典的阵线以匹配波斯人的阵线。

sentences.en: And he does this by thinning out the centre.
sentences.zh: 他通过削弱中心地带做到了这一点。

sentences.en: So the centre is given to three of the generals, one of whom is a young general called Themistocles, who will have an important role to play in subsequent Athenian history.
sentences.zh: 中心地带交给了三位将军，其中一位是年轻的将军地米斯托克利，他在随后的雅典历史中将扮演重要角色。

sentences.en: And he is stationed in the weakened centre.
sentences.zh: 他被部署在被削弱的中心。

sentences.en: Callimachus, the war archon, he commands the right wing.
sentences.zh: 军事执政官卡利马科斯指挥右翼。

sentences.en: That's the traditional place that the war archon stands.
sentences.zh: 那是军事执政官的传统站位。

sentences.en: And the Plataeans, in their leather helmets, are stationed on the left.
sentences.zh: 戴着皮头盔的普拉提亚人被部署在左翼。

sentences.en: So they are lined up.
sentences.zh: 于是他们列好了阵。

sentences.en: Sacrifice is offered.
sentences.zh: 祭祀已经完成。

sentences.en: The portents are good.
sentences.zh: 预兆很好。

sentences.en: Miltiades then stands where everyone can hear him.
sentences.zh: 米太亚得站在每个人都能听到的地方。

sentences.en: And he gives the command, at them.
sentences.zh: 他下达了命令：进攻。

sentences.en: And there's a great shimmering of metal as the hoplites lower their helmets.
sentences.zh: 随着重装步兵压下头盔，金属发出了一阵巨大的闪光。

sentences.en: They heft their shields.
sentences.zh: 他们举起盾牌。

sentences.en: And they shoulder their spears.
sentences.zh: 他们扛起长矛。

sentences.en: And you can imagine how terrifying this moment must be.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象这一刻是多么令人恐惧。

sentences.en: You know, you are a hoplite.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你是一名重装步兵。

sentences.en: Your head is now encased in metal.
sentences.zh: 你的头现在被金属包裹着。

sentences.en: You are effectively cut off from all the sounds around you.
sentences.zh: 你实际上与周围所有的声音隔绝了。

sentences.en: The trumpets are braying to signal the start of the advance, but you can barely hear it through the bronze of your helmet.
sentences.zh: 号角声吹响，发出进攻的信号，但你几乎无法透过头盔的青铜听到它。

sentences.en: But what you do have is the kind of this great collective jolting of the Athenian line as your fellows on to your left and to your right start the descent.
sentences.zh: 但你确实感受到了雅典阵线那巨大的集体震动，因为你左右的同伴开始了冲锋。

sentences.en: And so you have no choice.
sentences.zh: 所以你别无选择。

sentences.en: Even if you're an absolute coward, you still have to advance.
sentences.zh: 即使你是个彻头彻尾的懦夫，你也必须前进。

sentences.en: I think everyone on that morning must have felt terror.
sentences.zh: 我想那天早上每个人一定都感到了恐惧。

sentences.en: But I think that people in that advance are kind of born on the intoxication as well as the dread of the moment.
sentences.zh: 但我认为参与冲锋的人们既被那一刻的狂喜所支撑，也被那一刻的恐惧所驱使。

sentences.en: And, you know, we know that when Greeks advance into battle, there are those who wet themselves.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们知道当希腊人冲入战场时，确实有人会吓得尿裤子。

sentences.en: There are those who void their bowels and streak their cloaks.
sentences.zh: 有人会排泄出来，弄脏斗篷。

sentences.en: But you advance because you feel yourself to be part of a collective.
sentences.zh: 但你之所以前进，是因为你感到自己是集体的一部分。

sentences.en: You are kind of one with your fellow citizens.
sentences.zh: 你与你的公民同胞融为一体。

sentences.en: And I think that Herodotus, you know, we read it in the previous episode,
sentences.zh: 我想希罗多德，我们在上一集读到过，

sentences.en: that sense that being part of a democracy probably does give a sense of fellowship to an Athenian phalanx that perhaps hadn't previously existed.
sentences.zh: 那种身为民主制一部分的感觉，可能确实给雅典方阵带来了一种以前可能不存在的同袍情谊。

sentences.en: So as you descend down that slope onto the plain of Marathon, I think you probably do feel that you are part of a body of freeborn men.
sentences.zh: 所以当你沿着斜坡冲向马拉松平原时，我想你可能确实感到自己是一个自由人集体的一员。

sentences.en: I think that it would not be wrong to say that that is part of what steals the Athenians to take this, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想说这正是雅典人敢于冒这个险的原因之一，你知道，

sentences.en: this incredible risk of marching down to meet an enemy who has never been defeated by a Greek army before.
sentences.zh: 这种难以置信的冒险，去迎战一支从未被希腊军队击败过的敌人。

sentences.en: And they have a mile to cover.
sentences.zh: 他们有一英里的路程要走。

sentences.en: And incredible stories in due course come to be told of this advance.
sentences.zh: 关于这次冲锋，后来流传着不可思议的故事。

sentences.en: It's said that the Athenians ran the whole way down towards the Persian lines.
sentences.zh: 据说雅典人是一路跑向波斯阵线的。

sentences.en: I mean, this is impossible.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这不可能。

sentences.en: The weight of their kit is so heavy that they couldn't possibly have managed that and then fought a battle.
sentences.zh: 他们的装备太重了，他们不可能做到这一点还能进行战斗。

sentences.en: But I think it's clear that as they near the enemy, they do start to run.
sentences.zh: 但我认为很明显，当他们接近敌人时，他们确实开始奔跑了。

sentences.en: And Herodotus is very, very precise about this.
sentences.zh: 希罗多德对此描述得非常非常精确。

sentences.en: They were, he writes, so far as we can tell, the very first Greeks anywhere to make use of running towards an enemy as a tactic.
sentences.zh: 他写道，据我们所知，他们是希腊历史上第一批将“向敌人冲锋”作为战术的人。

sentences.en: And the first not to cringe before the sight of Median dress, so Persian dress, and the men who wear it.
sentences.zh: 也是第一批在看到米底服饰（即波斯服饰）和穿着它的人时没有退缩的人。

sentences.en: Hitherto, Greeks had only had to hear the name of the Medes to be reduced to a state of terror.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，希腊人只要听到米底人的名字就会陷入恐惧之中。

sentences.en: And they reach the Persian lines and they crash into the Persian lines and the impact is absolutely devastating.
sentences.zh: 他们到达了波斯阵线，猛烈地撞击进去，冲击力绝对是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: It's this great pulverizing smash up of metal into flesh and bone.
sentences.zh: 这是金属撞击血肉之躯的巨大粉碎声。

sentences.en: And the Persian forces are much more lightly armored than the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 波斯军队的装备比希腊人轻得多。

sentences.en: You know, they have probably quilted jerkins at beSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们充其量只有绗缝背心。

sentences.en: And this means that when the Athenians smash into them and they're using their spears, the spears don't shiver as they would if they were crashing into another phalanx.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当雅典人撞向他们并使用长矛时，长矛不会像撞上另一个方阵那样折断。

sentences.en: And that means that the Persians can be skewered and those who aren't skewered can be trampled underfoot by the sheer weight of all these bronze-clad men.
sentences.zh: 这意味着波斯人会被刺穿，而没被刺穿的人也会被这些身披青铜的士兵的巨大重量踩在脚下。

sentences.en: And then, of course, Dominic, you, I think with your expression, you conveyed a certain sense of skepticism as to whether Pan, with his curling goat horns and his enormous phallus,
sentences.zh: 当然，多米尼克，我想从你的表情中，你传达了一种怀疑，怀疑潘神，那个长着弯曲山羊角和巨大生殖器的神，

sentences.en: was going to turn up.
sentences.zh: 是否真的会出现。

sentences.en: I was a little skeptical.
sentences.zh: 我确实有点怀疑。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, he does turn up because the Persians are afflicted with a terrible sense of panic.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他确实出现了，因为波斯人陷入了一种可怕的恐慌之中。

sentences.en: And on the wings, they turn and they flee and they start scarpering for the boats, which are drawn up at the far end of the plain on the beach.
sentences.zh: 在侧翼，他们转身逃跑，开始向平原尽头海滩上的船只奔去。

sentences.en: And only in the center does the Persian force have the better of the fight because that's where the Athenian line has been weakened.
sentences.zh: 只有在中心地带，波斯军队占据了上风，因为那是雅典阵线被削弱的地方。

sentences.en: And also, it's where the best Persian troops are.
sentences.zh: 而且，那里也是波斯精锐部队所在的地方。

sentences.en: So the Persians themselves and also the Saka, the Scythians, who have these kind of enormous cleaving axes, like the House Karls at the Battle of Hastings.
sentences.zh: 所以波斯人自己，还有萨卡人（斯基泰人），他们拥有那种巨大的劈砍斧，就像黑斯廷斯战役中的皇家卫队一样。

sentences.en: And it looks briefly as though they might break through there.
sentences.zh: 看起来他们似乎很快就要在那里突破了。

sentences.en: But the Athenian wings who have sent the Persian wings fleeing, they are able to kind of curl around and to catch the Persians and the Saka on their flanks.
sentences.zh: 但已经击溃波斯侧翼的雅典侧翼部队，能够回旋过来，从侧面夹击波斯人和萨卡人。

sentences.en: And the Persian center then starts retreating and then panicking as well.
sentences.zh: 波斯中心部队也开始撤退，随后陷入恐慌。

sentences.en: And they're all streaming across the plain, running for the ships to try and get away.
sentences.zh: 他们全都涌向平原，奔向船只试图逃离。

sentences.en: So by this point, the battle is won.
sentences.zh: 所以到这一点，战斗已经赢了。

sentences.en: But it isn't yet over because, of course,
sentences.zh: 但战斗还没有结束，因为当然，

sentences.en: the fighting now moves to the ships because the Athenians are as desperate to stop the Persians from getting away as the Persians are to make their escape.
sentences.zh: 战斗现在转移到了船只上，因为雅典人阻止波斯人逃跑的决心，和波斯人想要逃跑的决心一样强烈。

sentences.en: And the Persians have the advantage, of course, that on their wings, the men who have broken there have a head start.
sentences.zh: 当然，波斯人有优势，因为在他们的侧翼，那些已经溃败的人有先发优势。

sentences.en: And so they are able to start piling into the ships before the Athenians arrive.
sentences.zh: 所以他们能在雅典人赶到之前开始涌向船只。

sentences.en: But once the Athenians get to the beach where all the Persian ships are drawn up, there is very, very desperate fighting.
sentences.zh: 但一旦雅典人到达停泊着所有波斯船只的海滩，战斗就变得非常非常惨烈。

sentences.en: And this, I'm sorry to say, is where the war archon dies.
sentences.zh: 很遗憾地说，军事执政官就是在这里牺牲的。

sentences.en: So Callimachus.
sentences.zh: 也就是卡利马科斯。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: Because the Athenians don't have this all their own way, do they?
sentences.zh: 因为雅典人并没有完全掌控局面，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, we don't want to give the impression that it's basically the Athenians completely wiping the floor with the Persians and the Persians doing nothing in response.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们不想给人留下一种印象，即雅典人基本上是完全碾压了波斯人，而波斯人毫无还手之力。

sentences.en: I mean, they're fighting pretty ferociously too.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们也打得非常凶猛。

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's on the beaches that the Athenian casualties are heavieSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以雅典人的伤亡最惨重的地方是在海滩上。

sentences.en: So we say Callimachus dies there, the war archon, another of the 10 generals, he dies there.
sentences.zh: 所以我们说卡利马科斯死在那里，另一位十将军之一也死在那里。

sentences.en: And there's a very famous story.
sentences.zh: 有一个非常著名的故事。

sentences.en: The one Athenian reaches up to the prow of a ship that is pulling away to try and stop it.
sentences.zh: 一名雅典人伸手去抓一艘正在驶离的船的船头，试图阻止它。

sentences.en: And there's a person with an axe who swings it down, chops off the Athenian's hand who collapses into the sea, blood spraying everywhere.
sentences.zh: 有一个人拿着斧头砍了下来，砍断了那名雅典人的手，他倒在海里，鲜血四溅。

sentences.en: And this Athenian is the brother of Aeschylus, who is the first of the three great Athenian tragedians of the 5th century BC.
sentences.zh: 这名雅典人是埃斯库罗斯的兄弟，埃斯库罗斯是公元前5世纪三位伟大的雅典悲剧作家中的第一位。

sentences.en: And Aeschylus himself is also fighting at Marathon.
sentences.zh: 埃斯库罗斯本人也参加了马拉松战役。

sentences.en: And he has this famous epitaph.
sentences.zh: 他有这句著名的墓志铭。

sentences.en: So when he dies, he doesn't mention any of his tragedies.
sentences.zh: 所以当他去世时，他没有提到他的任何悲剧作品。

sentences.en: He just said, you know, I was at Marathon.
sentences.zh: 他只是说，你知道，我参加了马拉松战役。

sentences.en: I fought against the long-haired mead.
sentences.zh: 我与长发的米底人战斗过。

sentences.en: That was the one thing that he was proud of.
sentences.zh: 那是他唯一引以为豪的事情。

sentences.en: So the Athenians do manage to capture some of the Persian ships to kind of burn them.
sentences.zh: 所以雅典人确实设法俘获了一些波斯船只并将其烧毁。

sentences.en: But the mass of the fleet does manage to pull away.
sentences.zh: 但大部分舰队确实设法逃脱了。

sentences.en: And so this is a problem for the Athenians because the question now is, well, where is it going to be heading?
sentences.zh: 这对雅典人来说是个问题，因为现在的问题是，它们要去哪里？

sentences.en: You know, Athens effectively stands defenseless.
sentences.zh: 你知道，雅典实际上处于毫无防备的状态。

sentences.en: And there's an even more alarming question.
sentences.zh: 还有一个更令人担忧的问题。

sentences.en: What about all that cavalry that had embarked and sailed off?
sentences.zh: 那些已经登船并驶离的骑兵怎么办？

sentences.en: And then, even as they're kind of, you know, worrying about these questions, something very, very alarming happens,
sentences.zh: 然后，就在他们还在担心这些问题的时候，发生了一件非常非常令人担忧的事情，

sentences.en: which is that up on the heights of Mount Pentelicon, the mountain that stands between Marathon and Athens, there's a flashing from a mirror or a shield.
sentences.zh: 那就是在马拉松和雅典之间的彭特利孔山高处，闪烁着镜子或盾牌的光芒。

sentences.en: And it's clearly a prearranged signal that is being delivered from someone in Athens, a traitor in Athens, signaling out to the Persian admirals.
sentences.zh: 这显然是有人从雅典发出的预先安排好的信号，雅典出了叛徒，正在向波斯海军将领通风报信。

sentences.en: And nobody knows who it is.
sentences.zh: 没人知道那个人是谁。

sentences.en: Nobody will ever know who it is.
sentences.zh: 永远也不会有人知道那个人是谁。

sentences.en: But it is evident that there is potential treachery afoot.
sentences.zh: 但显而易见，潜在的背叛正在酝酿之中。

sentences.en: And so the Athenian generals say, well, we cannot pause here.
sentences.zh: 于是雅典将军们说，好吧，我们不能在这里停下。

sentences.en: We can't, you know, rest on our laurels.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们不能躺在功劳簿上睡大觉。

sentences.en: We've got to get moving.
sentences.zh: 我们必须立刻出发。

sentences.en: And it's by now 10 o'clock in the morning.
sentences.zh: 此时已经是上午10点了。

sentences.en: The Athenians are obviously exhausted.
sentences.zh: 雅典人显然已经精疲力竭。

sentences.en: They're sweat-soaked.
sentences.zh: 他们浑身湿透，全是汗水。

sentences.en: They're wounded, covered in blood.
sentences.zh: 他们受了伤，浑身是血。

sentences.en: But all of them are thinking about their families and homes back in Athens.
sentences.zh: 但他们每个人心里想的都是远在雅典的家人和家园。

sentences.en: And so they decide we are going to have to march as fast as we can from Marathon and get back to Athens.
sentences.zh: 所以他们决定，必须以最快的速度从马拉松撤回雅典。

sentences.en: And there is, of course, a famous story that I'm sure most people will have heard, that they send Pheidippides, the runner, ahead of them to run the 26 miles back to Athens.
sentences.zh: 当然，有一个著名的故事，我相信大多数人都听说过，那就是他们派信使菲迪皮德斯先行一步，跑回26英里外的雅典。

sentences.en: And he gets there in record time and he proclaims, rejoice, we have won.
sentences.zh: 他以破纪录的时间赶到那里，高呼：欢呼吧，我们赢了。

sentences.en: And then he dies with the exhaustion and intoxication of the moment.
sentences.zh: 然后他因极度疲惫和那一刻的狂喜而倒地身亡。

sentences.en: Is this story true?
sentences.zh: 这个故事是真的吗？

sentences.en: It's not in Herodotus.
sentences.zh: 希罗多德的著作里没有记载。

sentences.en: It's in much later Greek sources.
sentences.zh: 它出现在更晚期的希腊文献中。

sentences.en: But, of course, this is what inspires the famous marathon race in the 1896 Olympics.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这正是1896年奥运会马拉松比赛的灵感来源。

sentences.en: So it might not be true.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能不是真的。

sentences.en: Might not be true.
sentences.zh: 可能不是真的。

sentences.en: I mean, I like to think it is.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我倒希望它是真的。

sentences.en: All these stories, I prefer to think that they are.
sentences.zh: 所有这些故事，我更愿意相信它们是真的。

sentences.en: And it means that the Battle of Marathon is the only battle to have an Olympic event.
sentences.zh: 这意味着马拉松战役是唯一一场拥有奥运比赛项目的战役。

sentences.en: But what we know for sure from Herodotus, whether Pheidippides has gone ahead of them or not, is that the Athenian army, I mean, to quote Herodotus,
sentences.zh: 但我们从希罗多德那里确切知道的是，无论菲迪皮德斯是否先行一步，雅典军队——引用希罗多德的话说——

sentences.en: they raced back to the defence of their city as fast as their legs could carry them.
sentences.zh: 他们以最快的速度奔回城中保卫家园。

sentences.en: And astonishingly, they arrived there by late afternoon.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，他们在傍晚时分就赶到了。

sentences.en: And it's just in the nick of time, because not long after they have turned up in Athens, the Persian fleet glides up towards Valerium, which is the harbour that serves Athens.
sentences.zh: 而且时间恰到好处，因为他们刚到雅典没多久，波斯舰队就滑向了雅典的港口法勒鲁姆。

sentences.en: And so the Athenians march down to Valerium.
sentences.zh: 于是雅典人向法勒鲁姆进发。

sentences.en: They draw themselves up in kind of great bronze lines.
sentences.zh: 他们排成了宏伟的青铜方阵。

sentences.en: And the Persian fleet lies stationary off the entrance to the harbour at Valerium.
sentences.zh: 波斯舰队停泊在法勒鲁姆港口外。

sentences.en: And then the sun sets, it's dusk, the Persian fleet raises anchor, swings round, and sails eastwards into the night.
sentences.zh: 随后太阳落山，暮色降临，波斯舰队起锚调头，向东驶入夜色之中。

sentences.en: And the threat of invasion is over.
sentences.zh: 入侵的威胁解除了。

sentences.en: And Athens is saved.
sentences.zh: 雅典得救了。

sentences.en: But the question, I suppose, is how long is it saved for?
sentences.zh: 但我认为问题在于，这种安宁能持续多久？

sentences.en: Now, we haven't yet talked about the Spartans.
sentences.zh: 我们还没谈到斯巴达人。

sentences.en: So the Spartans arrive shortly after the battle, don't they?
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人在战后不久就到了，对吧？

sentences.en: And they've been on the road for three days.
sentences.zh: 他们已经在路上走了三天了。

sentences.en: So they must be pretty exhausted themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以他们自己肯定也精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's an impressive march from them.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说是一次令人印象深刻的行军。

sentences.en: They're late, but they've still, you know, they've done well to get there.
sentences.zh: 他们迟到了，但能赶到那里已经很不容易了。

sentences.en: So great scenes.
sentences.zh: 场面很壮观。

sentences.en: They congratulate the Athenians.
sentences.zh: 他们向雅典人表示祝贺。

sentences.en: They go to the battlefield and they see there the 6,400 bodies of the fallen Persians.
sentences.zh: 他们来到战场，看到了6400具波斯阵亡者的尸体。

sentences.en: And it's an interesting scene, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这场景很有趣，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because the Spartans are very, they're fascinated by what the Persians are wearing, what kit they've got, what arms and armour.
sentences.zh: 因为斯巴达人对波斯人的穿着、装备、武器和盔甲非常着迷。

sentences.en: Because this is their first chance to look at what the most formidable people in the world have, what they've got.
sentences.zh: 因为这是他们第一次有机会观察世界上最强大的民族到底拥有什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a bit like, you know, we did the episode on the American attempt to rescue the hostages in Iran and the helicopter crashes.
sentences.zh: 是的，这有点像我们之前做的那期关于美国试图营救伊朗人质却导致直升机坠毁的节目。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, the Iranians inspect the helicopter because it's a way of trying to understand what the Americans can do.
sentences.zh: 你知道，伊朗人检查直升机是为了试图了解美国人的能力。

sentences.en: And I think the Spartans are exactly the same, that they're looking at the, you know, the armour and the arms and so on that the Persians have.
sentences.zh: 我认为斯巴达人也是一样，他们正在观察波斯人的盔甲和武器等等。

sentences.en: And to be honest, they're not very impressed.
sentences.zh: 老实说，他们印象并不深刻。

sentences.en: They think, well, you know, we could beat these any day.
sentences.zh: 他们心想，好吧，我们随时都能打败这些人。

sentences.en: But equally, I think the fact that the Spartans are so concerned to go and make this inspection
sentences.zh: 但同样，我认为斯巴达人如此关心并进行这次视察的事实，

sentences.en: is a reflection of the fact, not just that they've now woken up to just how major a threat
sentences.zh: 反映出他们不仅意识到波斯人是一个巨大的威胁，

sentences.en: the Persians are, but also this kind of nagging anxiety that even if the Persians have been defeated now at Marathon, you know, they probably will be back.
sentences.zh: 而且还有一种挥之不去的焦虑：即使波斯人在马拉松战役中被击败了，他们很可能还会卷土重来。

sentences.en: So we should try and, you know, get as much information on them as we possibly can.
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该尽可能多地收集关于他们的情报。

sentences.en: This raises an interesting question, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 这引出了一个有趣的问题，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because to the Greeks, the Battle of Marathon is an event that will echo through the centuries.
sentences.zh: 因为对希腊人来说，马拉松战役是一场将回响几个世纪的事件。

sentences.en: It's an absolutely seismic historical moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个绝对震撼的历史时刻。

sentences.en: But presumably to the Persians, you know, it's what, a sideshow at best?
sentences.zh: 但对波斯人来说，这充其量只是个小插曲吧？

sentences.en: Peripheral border skirmish, I think, is probably how they would have framed it.
sentences.zh: 我想他们大概会将其描述为一场边缘的边境冲突。

sentences.en: A border skirmish that didn't go the way that they had hoped, but such things happen when you're a superpower.
sentences.zh: 一场没能如愿的边境冲突，但作为超级大国，这种事难免会发生。

sentences.en: I think they probably wouldn't even have mentioned Marathon.
sentences.zh: 我想他们可能根本就不会提到马拉松。

sentences.en: I mean, the thing is that the Persians don't write history in the way, say, that Herodotus does.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，波斯人写历史的方式和希罗多德不同。

sentences.en: So we don't have any Persian accounts of any of the wars against the Greeks at all.
sentences.zh: 所以我们根本没有关于任何波斯对希腊战争的波斯方记录。

sentences.en: But Robert Graves, so as in I, Claudius, he wrote a fantastic poem called The Persian
sentences.zh: 但罗伯特·格雷夫斯，就是写《我，克劳迪亚斯》的那位，写过一首精彩的诗叫《波斯版本》，

sentences.en: Version, in which he imagines how the Persians would have spun the defeat at Marathon.
sentences.zh: 他在诗中想象了波斯人会如何粉饰马拉松的失败。

sentences.en: So just to quote from it, some of the lines, truth-loving Persians do not dwell upon the trivial skirmish fought near Marathon.
sentences.zh: 引用其中几句：热爱真理的波斯人不会纠结于马拉松附近那场微不足道的冲突。

sentences.en: Despite a strong defence and adverse weather, all arms combined magnificently together.
sentences.zh: 尽管防御坚固且天气恶劣，各兵种依然完美配合。

sentences.en: You know, superpowers never acknowledge the fact that they've been defeated.
sentences.zh: 你知道，超级大国从不承认自己被击败的事实。

sentences.en: Well, is it not?
sentences.zh: 嗯，难道不是吗？

sentences.en: I was thinking about this.
sentences.zh: 我一直在想这个问题。

sentences.en: It's the equivalent to them, probably, of a British defeat in Afghanistan or something in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 这大概相当于19世纪英国在阿富汗的失败之类的事件。

sentences.en: You know, sometimes these things happen on the frontier.
sentences.zh: 你知道，边境有时会发生这种事。

sentences.en: I think it's even better than that, because don't forget, they have actually captured Naxos,
